| [NOTE-013](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-013.md) | Quasi-quantization | Imposing a single "classical complementarity" restriction (you may only know jointly the values of Poisson-commuting quadrature variables) on a classical statistical theory reproduces a large part of quantum phenomenology, so any phenomenon arising in such an "epistricted" theory should be counted only weakly nonclassical. | Skimmed |

| [NOTE-017](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-017.md) | A structure theorem for generalized-noncontextual ontological models | In any diagram-preserving generalized-noncontextual ontological model of a tomographically local operational theory, the model must be an exact (non-overcomplete) frame representation of the associated GPT, so the number of ontic states equals the GPT dimension (for example exactly d² for a qudit). | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-018.md) | Why interference phenomena do not capture the essence of quantum theory | A classical statistical theory of discrete field modes with an epistemic restriction reproduces the standard Mach-Zehnder interference phenomenology (and bomb tester, delayed choice, quantum eraser), so interference by itself does not force wave-particle duality, observer-dependent reality or retrocausation. | Skimmed |
